### F02: Do not classify every failed camera direction as a clear sweep (P2)

retained operation-contract hole; not claimed a new gameplay regression

- [crates/adventuresim-tactical-client/src/camera/collision.rs:160](/home/brunosegovia/.codex/worktrees/ae46/adventure-simulator/target/bespoke-audit-774-merged-20261022/source/crates/adventuresim-tactical-client/src/camera/collision.rs:160)

Trace: Admitted Position<Scene> endpoints guarantee finite components ->
unchecked native subtraction/norm -> Dir3::new rejects -> CameraSweep returns
full fraction and no hit -> BoomRecovery::place accepts the endpoint. Zero
displacement and nonrepresentable geometry share that success path.

Counterexample: Opposite large finite endpoint/origin components can overflow
subtraction, or a finite displacement can overflow its norm. Both are admitted
by Position and can fail Dir3 construction; returning unobstructed is not a
checked failure. Ordinary zero displacement is a legitimate no-cast case.

Connected repair: Use the canonical checked displacement operation, explicitly
recognize zero-length casts, and reject nonfinite/overflowing displacement or
norm with CameraError. Only project to native direction/distance once geometry
is admitted. Audit the soft-occlusion cast in rig/observation.rs for the same
derived-norm contract.

Acceptance: Zero displacement remains a successful no-op; representability
failures return a cause and cannot commit a clear camera observation. Do not
silently impose a new arbitrary world bound.

Dependencies: canonical scene geometry; camera observation transaction.

Trace: Combatant.id admits a full u64 -> ScheduledMeleeTiming::attack_id shifts
left 32 and XORs quantized tick -> contact_batch finds rank by this truncated
identity -> timeline/cancellation evidence joins on the same raw key. Upper
combatant bits are discarded before the observer boundary.

Counterexample: Combatant IDs 1 and 4_294_967_297 with the same started tick
produce identical attack IDs. contact_batch.position selects the first matching
member for both, so both can receive order zero. Canceled/contacted joins can
also associate another actor's attack. This is a source/arithmetic proof, not an
executed test.

Connected repair: Mint a collision-free attack identity retaining the complete
combatant identity and actual attack instance (e.g. a composite or checked
allocated sequence). Carry that owner through retained schedule, attack batches,
affected-attack fields, timeline and evidence joins. Distinguish
batch/member/ordinal roles; do not fix by narrowing all combatant IDs to 32
bits.

Acceptance: Distinct full-width combatants and distinct admitted attack
instances cannot alias; simultaneous membership rank is unique in its batch;
cancellation/contact joins use the same retained identity. Existing ordering and
seed sampling are preserved.

Dependencies: core autoresolve attack identity; timeline payload and batch
membership; native causal evidence consumers.

validate_player_input checks finite components, then normalizes an optional
direction and filters zero out. At bevy_math0.19.1's pinned glam0.32.1
dependency, Vec2 length is sqrt(dot(self,self)); normalize_or returns fallback

ordinary-jump branch at player_projection.rs1326, setting
accumulated_input.jumped. This is reachable from a decoded request; no assertion
of normal keyboard production or a privilege bypass. Movement clamp has a
related finite-norm case but is not silently promoted into this finding without
policy analysis.

Connected repair: Admit jump intent once into an owning named state such as
OrdinaryJump versus Quickstep(QuickstepDirection); reject an invalid present
direction rather than collapse it into absence. Reuse canonical
animation::QuickstepDirection through validated input, DefendRequest/domain
defense intent, begin_authoritative_quickstep and QuickstepPush admission/state,
with scalar Vec2 only at actual wire/native transform/force kernels. Do not
repeatedly normalize raw Vec2 between internal functions. Preserve explicit
zero-input policy and ordinary-jump behavior deliberately; a robust finite
normalization alternative must likewise never relabel a rejected quickstep as
another action. Coordinate typed jump-edge chronology with M08. Trace all
action_direction recipients (motor, locomotion, procedural pose, accumulated
input and diagnostics) and active/inactive actuator representation before
completing the family.

Acceptance: A present but inadmissible quickstep cannot enqueue an ordinary
jump; None remains the intentional ordinary-jump request. Normal valid
directions and current4,-3→.8,-.6 fixture preserve orientation and timing.
Consumed edge behavior during incapacity/airborne intervals remains unchanged;
no repeated stale edge on recovery. Preserve current finite/zero/frame policy
explicitly and existing checks only; no new tests authorized.

Dependencies: M08 distinct jump/posture edge sequences; canonical
QuickstepDirection and DodgeSpec; QuickstepPush lifecycle/rollback
serialization; server defense ingress and fixed motor; native glam normalization
and explicit input policy.

zero/ephemeral mode. Propagate a structured allocation failure to the owning
request callback. Coordinate allocation timing with successful request admission

Trace: The GLB encoder receives actual serialized JSON and binary payload byte
vectors, rounds both lengths up to four-byte alignment, sums the header/chunk
extents as usize and writes total_length/json_bytes.len()/bytes.len() with
unchecked as u32 casts. Native u32 words are the real format boundary, but
neither alignment/sum overflow nor representability of each chunk and complete
container is established before those projections. A sufficiently large admitted
payload can therefore produce a truncated header or overflow the host arithmetic
instead of an owning error. Current bounded ordinary MHR exports have not been
proved to reach this limit; no huge allocation or file was created in this
audit.

Connected repair: At the actual encoder boundary, admit one checked GLB layout
covering padding, both chunk extents and the complete container, and reject host
arithmetic or native32-bit representation failure before
resizing/copying/writing. Keep checked lengths through the shared
layout/encoder; emit raw u32 only when writing header words. Use a focused
native-format layout/error contract rather than a naked cast or arbitrary
smaller global export cap. Reuse byte-unit concepts where semantics fit, but do
not equate this format32-bit limit with GPU buffer/device or word-count
contracts. Propagate failure through the owning structured export error M20.

Acceptance: All header extents equal the actual padded output size and are
natively representable; unsupported extents return a structured error before an
invalid file or partial output is emitted. Preserve byte-identical valid small
exports, exact padding/token/endian behavior and native IO causes. No invented
memory/workload policy and no claim that current ordinary assets overflow. Use
existing fixtures only after repairs are authorized; no new tests.

BufferBuilder/GLB/native file layout and caller admission trace; existing
four-byte padding, chunk constants and little-endian format output.

Source reasoning and arithmetic counterexamples were not executed as new tests.
Existing tests were read as evidence; no project checks were run. Historical CI
and previous reviewer verdicts do not clear this audit. The saved hosted status
is only an observation made earlier at the PR head, not a claim that the run is
still running or that it passed.
